text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
FRONT PAGE POLITICAL NEWS
RZECZPOSPOLITA

- Former Polish president Lech Walesa will canvass for the Solidarity Electoral Action (AWS) in the forthcoming parliamentary elections, Lech Walesa and AWS leader Marian Krzaklewski agreed yesterday.

- The centrist opposition Union for Freedom (UW) party will challenge the newly proposed tax law at the Constitutional Tribunal when the bill becomes law, claiming that it puts an unecessary burden on tax payers and tax offices, UW leader Leszek Balcerowicz said.
ECONOMIC AND MARKET NEWS
RZECZPOSPOLITA

- Japan's Isuzu Motors Limited has received an operating licence to produce at an Isuzu diesel engine plant to be built in the Katowice special economic zone in southern Poland, Izusu president Kazuhira Seki said.
Isuzu is planning to invest up to $350 million in the plant to employ over 500 workers.
- Around 44.1 percent of Poles are planning to buy a passenger car in the next three years and 18.3 percent plan to do so this year, a survey by the CBM market research firm showed.
Around 48.5 percent of the surveyed Poles will apply for bank credit to finance the purchase.
- A new railway connection between Poznan, western Poland, and Berlin will be launched by the Polish State Railways (PKP) and Deutsche Bahn AG on June 1, 1997.

- The Centertel analogue mobile phone operator, controlled by state-owned telecoms monopolist Telekomunikacja Polska SA (TPSA), made a net profit of 253.4 million zlotys in 1996, 38.8 percent growth compared with 1995, a Centertel preliminary report said.

- Poland's industrial development agency (ARP), which administers the special economic zone in Mielec, will invest 10 million zlotys in infrastructure modernisation and development this year, ARP said.
- The ZPC Wawel SA confectionery maker in Krakow will present a share issue prospectus to the Polish Securities Commission (KPW) in June this year.
The company plans to sell between 600,000 and one million shares priced at five zlotys each in a public offering this autumn, Wawel said.

- The date of the final agreement with a planned strategic investor for Powszechny Bank Kredytowy (PBK) has been put off until the end of the month, the bank's privatisation adviser HSBC Investment Services said.

- The Unimil contraceptive maker's general shareholders meeting has decided to raise share capital to 10.18 million zlotys and to present a share issue prospectus to the Polish Securities Commission (KPW) in June.
Unimil is a subsidiary of the listed Universal foreign trade firm.
- A general shareholders meeting of the Compensa insurance firm has decided to put the company's 1996 net profit of 2.2 million zlotys into the firm's reserve capital.
DZIENNIK PRAWA I GOSPODARKI
- Poland's unemployment rate fell to 12.4 percent in April, Labour Minister Tadeusz Zielinski said.
- Sales of the Delphi Automotive Systems (DAS) vehicle component maker plants in Poland reached $40 million in 1996 and are doubling each year, DAS regional director Leszek Waliszewski said.

- The listed Stalexport foreign trade firm has sued the state treasury in the Katowice provincial court for a return of 52 million zlotys of overpaid in taxes in 1989 and 1990 due to currency exchange differences.
GAZETA WYBORCZA

- Polish banks will have to cut operating costs by 50 percent to compete successfully with western banks on the domestic market following the sector's liberalisation in 1999, the central bank's former president Wladyslaw Jaworski said.
ZYCIE

- Damages paid out to Polish insurance firms in 1996 exceeded premiums by 375 million zlotys, the state insurance supervision office (PUNU) president Danuta Walcerz said. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
